title: A fixed 16.34-day phase fit does not improve later peak-frequency predictions for FRB 20180916B in CHIME Catalog 2
abstract: We test whether the known activity phase of FRB 20180916B predicts fitted burst peak frequency in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231. A linear fit uses 84 events before 2022. Its error on 19 later events is 85.7 MHz RMS, compared with 80.1 MHz for the early mean. Thus its mean squared error is 14.5 percent larger. The early phase slope is negative, but the later interval includes zero. A cycle bootstrap gives a broad interval for forecast skill. Harmonic fits and signal-strength and flagged-channel controls also fail to improve the later forecast at the fixed published period. Period uncertainty and a small later sample limit this result. It does not reject known frequency-dependent activity across radio bands. No new source or physical signal is confirmed. Code, selected data, source hashes, all diagnostic tables, figures, and offline instructions are included.

display.caption: Peak frequency versus fixed activity phase, and the early linear forecast for later events.
